neighbours.label: the 'ettle/tle' piece of 'nettle(s)' (stinging nettle), a plant-name compound piece
fire: In early spring we gathered young stinging nettles for soup along the riverbank.
The garden path was overgrown with nettles, so we wore long trousers.
Herbalists often brew nettle tea to ease seasonal allergies.
My ankles brushed against a patch of nettle and burned for an hour.
Butterflies lay their eggs on nettles growing near the hedge.
She cooked a creamy risotto with wild nettle leaves and garlic.
Old ropes were once woven from the fibres of the common nettle.
Wear gloves when you pull out stinging nettles from the vegetable bed.
quiet: In early spring we gathered young dandelion leaves for soup along the riverbank.
The garden path was overgrown with brambles, so we wore long trousers.
Herbalists often brew chamomile tea to ease seasonal allergies.
My ankles brushed against a patch of thistle and stung for an hour.
Butterflies lay their eggs on milkweed growing near the hedge.
She cooked a creamy risotto with wild spinach leaves and garlic.
Old ropes were once woven from the fibres of the common hemp plant.
Wear gloves when you pull out prickly weeds from the vegetable bed.

notes: card only; top examples mix nettle, holdfast, concealed carry, cover crops; testing the commonest one (nettle)
